examples.title: VISL calculator, resident at the form defaults, from the calculator's printed inputs
examples.source: Vapor Intrusion Screening Level User's Guide
examples.compares: The calculator output for five chemicals (benzene, trichloroethylene, tetrachloroethylene, naphthalene, ethylbenzene; resident, groundwater at 25 deg C, hazard quotient 0.1, target risk 1e-6), retrieved 2026-10-22: the engine is run from the properties, toxicity values and exposure inputs the calculator prints for the run, which checks the engine's equations. Compared: the cancer and noncancer target indoor air levels and the governing one, the sub-slab and near-source soil gas level, the groundwater level, the pure phase and maximum groundwater vapor concentrations, H prime used, and the yes or no answers. All 65 printed cells: 62 reproduce, 3 are excepted (the trichloroethylene cancer level, which the calculator takes from the RSL equations for that chemical, and the tetrachloroethylene groundwater level and H prime, which miss by less than the rounding of the printed inputs), 0 are unexplained.

defaults.subject: Foster and Chrostowski film reference coefficients (3000 cm/h gas, 20 cm/h liquid)
defaults.note: RISC5 choices that could not be verified against the primary paper; they are inputs and the defaults are warned. The stagnant stall source is a planned, unverified record and is not cited.

defaults.subject: Little (1992) two-resistance stall mass balance
defaults.note: The mass balance is our statement of the two-resistance theory, checked by limit identities; it is not a transcription of the paper.

defaults.subject: Household transfer factor K (RSL whole-house water-to-air term)
defaults.note: An entered value, not verified against a primary page of the RSL documentation. Table 1 of the archived RSL User's Guide (19january2021snapshot.epa.gov/risk/regional-screening-levels-rsls-users-guide_.html, read 2026-10-21) lists K, the Andelman volatilization factor, as 0.5 L/m3, citing U.S. EPA 1991b (pg. 20). The page prints its equations as images, so the form (C_a = C_w K) was not read from it. Numerically, K = 0.5 reproduces 263 of the 265 tap water inhalation levels of the RSL November 2024 table (the resident air level divided by K; the two misses are the trichloroethylene and vinyl chloride cancer cells, which the RSL computes with its own equations; see the tap water sweep above). That is consistency with the published table, not verification from a primary source, so the warning stays.

defaults.subject: HHRAP fallback standing in for Trapp (2015)
defaults.note: The modern plant model is the EPA HHRAP 2005 produce equations until the Trapp (2015) models are read.

defaults.subject: Transpiration stream concentration factor (TSCF) and leaf-air partition coefficient
defaults.note: User inputs, because their published regressions were not read.

defaults.subject: Briggs root concentration factor constants
defaults.note: The constants 0.77 and -1.52 were read in the paper itself on 2026-10-21 (Pestic. Sci. 13, 495-504, open copy in the Rothamsted repository, page 500, Equations 1 and 2; the TSCF equation is on page 502). The engine's form drops the paper's 0.82 term above log Kow 2, as the HHRAP appendix does: Equation 1 is the macerated-root line, and Equation 2 adds 0.82 to the root concentration factor at every log Kow.

defaults.subject: Schulze-Makuch (2005) dispersivity coefficients
defaults.note: The unconsolidated-media pair c = 0.20, m = 0.44 is quoted from lecture notes that cite the paper, not from the paper’s own tables.

defaults.subject: Gelhar et al. (1985) two-branch vadose dispersivity regression
defaults.note: The coefficients have no primary source located: the EPRI report (EA-4190, full text read 2026-10-21) prints no regression equation, only field data and a plot against scale. They come from RISC5’s statement of its choice. The reference stays cited for the field data compilation it does contain.

defaults.subject: Gelhar et al. (1985) saturated-zone log-quadratic dispersivity regression
defaults.note: The coefficients of ln(aL) = -3.795 + 1.774 ln x - 0.093 (ln x)^2 have no primary source located: the EPRI report (EA-4190) prints no regression equation, only field data and a plot against scale. They come from RISC5’s statement of its choice. The reference stays cited for the field data compilation it does contain.

defaults.subject: Organic Koc and H of the SSG 1996 Table A-1 fixture
defaults.note: The nine organic Koc values (Table 39, calculated Koc) and H (Table 36, dimensionless) were read from the primary document on 2026-10-21 and match, after correcting PCE H to 0.754. Table C-1 of the User's Guide and the inorganic Kd values were not re-read.

notChecked.subject: RSL soil inhalation cells
notChecked.note: The soil inhalation levels of the RSL tables (435 cells each for resident and industrial soil) and the soil totals that include them (another 435 each) are not checked: they rest on the RSL volatilization and particulate emission factors, which the November 2024 sweep does not compute. The sweeps check tap water inhalation and the industrial air levels; the 30-case independent check does not. The benzo(a)pyrene tap water dermal value is omitted by the RSL and has no case.

notChecked.subject: RSL sweep cells that do not reproduce
notChecked.note: Unexplained: the tap water total cancer level of Aroclor 1242, 1248, 1254 and 1260 (printed 0.0078 ug/L, computed 0.007852 ug/L; no reason found). Excepted with a reason: the trichloroethylene and vinyl chloride cancer cells (the RSL special-case equations), lead (key G, no toxicity value in the database) and refractory ceramic fibers (key G, database value in fibers). The counts are in the sweep entries above.

notChecked.subject: DeVaull (2007) vapor model
notChecked.note: No published numeric example could be verified, so the model rests on identities and hand cases built from independent closed forms. There is no fixture file.

notChecked.subject: Table R-9 pages 2 and 3
notChecked.note: The RISC5 guide reproduces only page 1 of the three pages, so the other rows cannot be checked.
